root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted: Pietrowsky Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 Nc6

overview: In the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted Black plays 5...Nc6 instead of ...e6, ...c6 or ...g6. White develops with Bb5 or Bc4, Bf4 and Qe2 or Qd2 and tries to use the f-file and Bg5, aiming at Black's king. Black can consolidate by giving back the pawn but White's compensation is not sound against accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bb5, Bf4 and Qe2 and castle long or short
Attack down the f-file and aim at f7 and g7

black_ideas.idea: Hold the extra pawn and complete development with ...Bg4 and ...e6

typical_structures.structure: Open position with a White lead in development
Black pawn on e-file or c6 supported by pieces

character.notes: A gambit tactical fight with White hoping for an early attack.

gambit.notes: White is a pawn down after 4...exf3 5.Nxf3 and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Engines favour Black; White's compensation is insufficient.

structure.notes: The centre opens and play is on open files.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom use the BDG at all.

level.notes: Sharp theory needed but dubious so not a good first repertoire.

character.reason: Open gambit play with fast attacks and tactics.

soundness.reason: Engines and masters judge White's compensation insufficient.

structure.reason: Pieces fight on open files and diagonals.
